title: Measuring Verifier Impact in an LLM Generate→Verify→Repair Loop for Intent→Configuration NetOps Tasks
abstract: We quantify how inserting a deterministic network verifier plus a single automated repair iteration into a generate→verify→repair loop changes verifier-detected safety violations for LLM-produced device-configuration proposals. In a preregistered paired design (N = 500 intent→configuration tasks stratified across VLAN-change, ACL-change, and static-route-change clusters) we used shared_initial_candidate semantics: a single LLM proposal per task (requested model: gpt-5-mini) was recorded and then either (baseline) accepted as-is or (guarded) passed to a deterministic validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) which invoked at most one automated repair call when a preregistered high/medium-severity violation was found. Complete pairs = 500; baseline passed 499/500 (0.998), guarded passed 500/500 (1.000); contingency: n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002; paired-bootstrap 95% percentile CI = [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). The preregistered exact McNemar two-sided test was computed as an exact binomial on discordant pairs (n = n10 + n01) yielding two-sided p = 1.00 for the observed n10 = 1, n01 = 0. Execution accounting: model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage calls = 1. Interpretation: on this verifier-scoped synthetic corpus and the chosen model+validator pairing, the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals; therefore the measurable marginal pass-rate improvement from a single verifier+repair iteration is small, though the archived run includes one concrete corrected baseline failure. We document design choices, statistical rules, execution accounting, provenance pointers, and limitations; all artifacts (prompts, responses, validator traces, provider-call traces, preregistration, and analysis logs) are archived in the evidence bundle referenced in the Disclosure Statement.

sections.introduction: Generative large language models (LLMs) are being integrated into NetOps workflows to translate human intent into device configuration, plan multi-step changes, and propose repairs. Operational deployments and surveys emphasize that safety and correctness often depend on surrounding engineering—deterministic validators, sandbox replay, canarying, and rollback—rather than on the model alone [Beckett et al., 2017; Wei et al., 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. A prevalent mitigation pattern is generate→verify→repair (G→V→R): an LLM produces a candidate configuration, a deterministic verifier checks formalized properties, and repairs are applied automatically or via human oversight. Despite conceptual adoption, there is limited controlled, artifact-backed measurement isolating the verifier’s marginal contribution when the model’s initial proposal is held fixed. We therefore preregistered and executed a paired experiment to answer a narrowly scoped operational question: given identical initial proposals (shared_initial_candidate semantics), how many verifier-detected safety violations are avoided by adding a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration compared to using the LLM proposal alone?
sections.related_work: Deterministic network-configuration verification (header-space and route-model verifiers) can check reachability, isolation, and update-safety and form the basis of many NetOps verification tools [Beckett et al., 2017]. Recent system papers describe LLM-driven intent translators and stress the importance of validators and guardrails for operational reliability [INTA, 2025; Confucius, 2025; Bilal et al., 2026]. Generate–verify–repair and critic-in-the-loop architectures are proposed for structured generation and operational tasks beyond networking [PoeTone; INTA]. Failure-mode analyses of LLM-driven automation document hallucination, overconfidence, and integration failure modes that motivate verifier-in-the-loop designs [Owen, 2026; DeepSeek-AI, 2025]. However, the supplied literature rarely presents controlled ablations that quantify a verifier’s effect size under reproducible preregistered conditions; our study contributes one such artifact-backed measurement and situates its conditional scope relative to prior work.
sections.methodology:
Preregistration and confirmatory plan: We preregistered study_id cand_7f4b9a2d_hosted_gvr_v1_2026 and froze the primary estimand, inclusion/exclusion rules, task-generator seeds, analysis executor (paired_binary_analysis_v1), multiplicity plan, retry policy, and stopping rule before execution. Confirmatory hypothesis H1: an LLM paired with a deterministic verifier plus a single automated repair iteration will produce a lower verifier-detected safety-violation rate than the LLM alone (paired within-task). Success is defined as verifier reporting zero preregistered high/medium-severity violations on the property set modeled by the validator.

Task generation and strata: We generated a deterministic synthetic corpus of 500 intent→configuration tasks using deterministic_netops_task_generator_v5 with preregistered seeds and stratified allocation: VLAN-change (167 tasks), ACL-change (167), static-route-change (166). Each task contains explicit initial_state, expected_final_state, allowed_fields (constrained to {admin, mtu, vlan}), and required_sequence. Tasks referencing features the verifier did not model would have been routed to an 'unmodeled-feature' cohort and excluded by pre-specified rules; no confirmatory exclusions occurred.

Generation semantics and experimental control: The preregistered generation_semantics = "shared_initial_candidate" with independent_condition_generation = false. For each task the pipeline produced a single shared LLM proposal (requested model: gpt-5-mini). That shared candidate served as the baseline output; the guarded arm evaluated that identical shared candidate with deterministic_netops_validator_v5 and invoked the repair-stage call only if the validator reported a preregistered high/medium-severity violation. This design isolates the marginal effect of verification+repair conditional on identical model proposals and avoids conflation with verifier-driven regeneration or independent guarded-generation strategies.

Models, adapter, and validator: Requested LLM = gpt-5-mini (provider recorded as openai_responses) called via hosted_netops_gvr_v1 adapter. Model configuration (execution/model_configuration.json) specified max_output_tokens = 2000 and single-attempt generation. The validator used for gating and final scoring was deterministic_netops_validator_v5; the validator-spec and its mapping of violation codes to severity levels are archived with the execution artifacts.

Statistical tests and exact implementation: The preregistered primary confirmatory test is McNemar’s paired test on binary pass/fail outcomes. Our archived analysis executor implements the exact two-sided McNemar as an exact binomial on the number of discordant pairs n = n10 + n01: under H0 each discordant outcome is equally likely, so X ∼ Binomial(n, 0.5) and the two-sided p-value is p_two_sided = 2 × min{P(X ≤ n10), P(X ≥ n10)}, truncated at 1.0. This implementation detail (exact-binomial-on-discordants) is archived in analysis/analysis_log.jsonl. We report the exact two-sided p-value and a paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI computed with B = 10,000 resamples (bootstrap_seed = 1729) resampling at the task/pair unit while preserving pairing.
sections.results:
Execution accounting and primary outcomes: The run completed with completed_episode_count = 1000 (500 pairs recorded under shared-initial semantics plus one repair-stage call) and model_calls_used = 501. Observed repair-stage provider calls = 1. Aggregated per-condition successes: baseline_success_count = 499 (baseline_success_rate = 0.998), guarded_success_count = 500 (guarded_success_rate = 1.0). Paired contingency table (guarded × baseline): n11 = 499, n10 = 1, n01 = 0, n00 = 0. Absolute paired success-rate difference (guarded − baseline) = 0.002. Analysis artifacts (analysis/condition_summary.csv and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv) encode these counts.

Exact McNemar two-sided result and CI: With discordant counts n = 1 (n10 = 1, n01 = 0), the archived exact-binomial rule yields two one-sided tail probabilities of 0.5, giving p_two_sided = 2×0.5 = 1.0 (conventional truncation yields p = 1.00). The paired-bootstrap percentile 95% CI for the absolute difference is [0.0, 0.006] (B = 10,000, seed = 1729). Both the exact p-value and bootstrap CI are stored in analysis/results.json and analysis/paired_contingency_table.csv.

Discordant-pair provenance and repair activity: Observed repair-stage calls = 1 and that single repair call produced the sole discordant outcome (n10 = 1), i.e., the guarded arm converted one baseline-detected violation into a verified pass. The artifact bundle archives per-task validator diagnostics, normalized configurations, repair prompts/responses (when invoked), and provider-call traces. Because the execution manifest and raw-results file (execution/raw_results.jsonl; sha256 recorded in the execution manifest) are the deterministic canonical sources, the discordant episode is locatable by filtering execution/raw_results.jsonl for pairs where baseline scoring indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) and guarded scoring indicates pass == 1. The validator violation-code→severity mapping and the repair-stage provider-call trace for that episode are present in the archived artifacts; these allow deterministic inspection and qualitative failure-mode analysis without manual adjudication. (Per the run’s archival practice we do not reproduce raw provider-call contents inline; instead the run provides deterministic artifact locations.)

Secondary analyses and power implications: Planned secondary per-violation-class analyses were uninformative because observed violation counts were near zero; there were no meaningful counts for class-level inference. Preregistered power calculations had assumed baseline error prevalence p_b ≈ 0.30; the observed baseline prevalence (1/500 failures) deviated dramatically, producing a ceiling effect that eliminates statistical power to detect small absolute gains on the pass-rate metric. This mismatch between planning assumptions and observed prevalence is captured in the preregistration and in the analysis logs and is discussed below as a principal threat to interpretability.
sections.discussion:
Operational interpretation: This confirmatory measurement is conditional: it quantifies verifier+single-repair impact under shared_initial_candidate semantics, a single requested model (gpt-5-mini), a deterministic validator limited to a constrained feature set (allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}), and a single automated repair iteration. In that regime the model’s proposals were nearly perfect, so the measurable pass-rate gain was small (0.002). However, the verifier demonstrated corrective potential by converting at least one concrete baseline failure into a pass (the archived discordant episode described above). In production deployments where baseline proposal error prevalence is higher, the verifier’s marginal benefit on pass-rate or other operational metrics could be substantially larger.

Design-choice implications: The shared_initial_candidate generation semantics were chosen to isolate verifier+repair effect conditional on identical proposals. This answers the operational question: what marginal safety gain does a verifier+single-repair provide when the model’s initial proposal is fixed? It does not measure the effect of verifier-guided regeneration, iterative repair loops, or larger repair budgets; practitioners should select generation semantics matching their operational priorities (minimize number of model calls vs maximize final pass rate). The archive contains alternative execution semantics and artifacts that would support follow-on experiments under different semantics.

Statistical interpretation and the observed p = 1.00: The exact two-sided McNemar implementation used here reduces to an exact-binomial test on discordant pairs. For n = 1 discordant pair the two-sided rule yields p = 1.00 because both one-sided tail probabilities are 0.5 and the two-sided p is 2×min{0.5,0.5} truncated at 1.0. This numeric result is a property of the small discordant count and the chosen exact test convention; it does not imply that the single correction is irrelevant operationally—rather, it reflects the limited sample evidence for asymmetry in discordant outcomes given the near-ceiling baseline. The paired-bootstrap CI [0.0, 0.006] quantifies uncertainty in the absolute difference under resampling and similarly expresses that any true effect on the pass-rate metric is small under observed conditions.

Threats to validity and limitations: Internal validity is supported by the preregistered paired design, deterministic generator seeds, and automated exclusion rules; no manual adjudication occurred. Construct validity is limited by the validator’s modeled property set: the pass/fail outcome is a composite relative to those modeled properties and severity mappings. External validity is constrained by a single requested model, a single deterministic validator, synthetic deterministic tasks limited to three task clusters, and allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}; results do not generalize to cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, richer protocol-state properties, or other models. The observed ceiling effect (499/500 baseline passes) invalidates the preregistered power assumptions and explains the negligible absolute improvement on the pass-rate metric. All these threats and their artifact evidence are documented in the execution and analysis manifests.

Operational recommendations: (1) Measure baseline proposal error prevalence on representative operational data before allocating repair budgets—when baseline error is very low, marginal pass-rate gains from an expensive verifier+repair pipeline on the pass-rate metric may be small. (2) Ensure verifier property coverage aligns with operator-critical constraints; validator-spec artifacts in the bundle document coverage and severity mapping. (3) Select generation semantics aligned with deployment goals: shared_initial semantics isolate marginal verifier effect per-proposal, whereas verifier-guided regeneration or iterative repair optimizes final-pass probability at the expense of additional model calls and latency.

Reproducibility and artifact grounding: All preregistration materials, task-generator seeds and code, model-configuration, provider-call traces, raw LLM responses, validator traces, repair prompts/responses, execution logs, and analysis CSVs are archived in the evidence bundle (execution/* and analysis/*). Key execution accounting recorded model_calls_used = 501 and observed repair-stage calls = 1. The archived initial master prompt is referenced in the Disclosure Statement with its immutable path and SHA-256. The single discordant episode can be located deterministically in execution/raw_results.jsonl by filtering for baseline pass == 0 and guarded pass == 1; that file contains the validator violation codes and the repair-stage prompt/response necessary for qualitative failure-mode analysis. We intentionally do not reproduce raw provider-call contents in the paper; the archived artifact bundle provides deterministic deterministic retrieval for audit and inspection.
sections.conclusion: We executed a preregistered, artifact-backed paired experiment (N = 500) that isolated the verifier+single-repair effect under shared_initial_candidate semantics. On a synthetic verifier-scoped corpus and with the requested model/validator pairing the LLM produced near-ceiling proposals (baseline 499/500; guarded 500/500), yielding an absolute improvement of 0.002 (95% CI [0.0, 0.006]; archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 under the two-sided binomial convention implemented). The result documents a ceiling-effect regime: when baseline proposal error prevalence is extremely low and verifier coverage is constrained, the measurable marginal pass-rate benefit of a single verifier+repair iteration on this metric may be negligible, while the verifier can still correct rare but concrete failures. Operators should measure baseline prevalence and align verifier coverage and generation semantics with operational priorities. All claims are supported by archived artifacts for deterministic reinspection.

limitations: Synthetic, deterministic task corpus limited to features modeled by the deterministic validator; task payloads constrained to allowed_fields = {admin, mtu, vlan}. Results do not necessarily generalize to unconstrained production intents, cross-vendor CLI heterogeneity, or protocol semantics outside the verifier scope.
Single requested model (gpt-5-mini) and single validator (deterministic_netops_validator_v5) were tested — no claim of multi-model or cross-validator generality.

Maximum one automated repair iteration was permitted by the preregistration; different repair budgets, iterative repair, or verifier-guided regeneration strategies could change measured verifier impact.

Very high baseline pass rate (499/500) produced a ceiling effect that limits power to detect small absolute improvements on the pass-rate metric; the archived exact McNemar two-sided p = 1.00 reflects the two-sided exact-binomial convention for n = 1 discordant pair and should be interpreted in that context.

The single discordant episode (the sole task where baseline failed and guarded succeeded) and its validator diagnostics and repair-stage trace are archived in execution/raw_results.jsonl in the evidence bundle. To inspect it deterministically: filter execution/raw_results.jsonl for pair entries where the baseline scoring outcome indicates a preregistered high/medium-severity violation (baseline pass == 0) while the guarded scoring outcome indicates pass == 1; because only one such discordant pair exists in the confirmatory set, this lookup returns the single episode and its provider-call traces. The validator violation-code→severity mapping is archived in the execution manifest and validator-spec artifacts in the bundle.
